Yes—there are several concrete improvements worth making. The browser capture → scene document → Penpot importer separation is useful, but some captured information never reaches the resulting layers.

I’d prioritize these findings:

1. **Container background images disappear.** Containers use `createContainerBackdrop()`, which only applies paint; image uploading happens in `createShape()`, which containers bypass. A hero section with a background photo and heading will lose the photo. Share asset-fill handling between ordinary shapes, container backdrops, and the root board. [penpot.ts:336](/home/peterc/ultimate-html-penpot-ext/src/importer/penpot.ts:336)

2. **Nested overflow clipping is lost.** Containers become groups, while clipping is applied only to boards. Cards with `overflow: hidden` therefore won’t clip their children. Use a clipping-capable representation where needed, preserving the captured bounds. [penpot.ts:68](/home/peterc/ultimate-html-penpot-ext/src/importer/penpot.ts:68)

3. **Transparency is applied incorrectly.** `cssColor()` discards RGBA alpha, so translucent backgrounds and shadows become opaque. Separately, solid shapes receive CSS opacity on both their fill and the shape itself—`opacity: .5` can produce a `.25` background contribution. Preserve color alpha independently and apply element opacity once. [penpot.ts:21](/home/peterc/ultimate-html-penpot-ext/src/importer/penpot.ts:21)

4. **CSS stacking order is ignored.** The extractor records `zIndex`, but rendering follows scene/DOM order without consulting it. Overlapping positioned elements can appear in the wrong order. This needs stacking-context-aware ordering; simply sorting every node by `z-index` would also be incorrect. [penpot.ts:327](/home/peterc/ultimate-html-penpot-ext/src/importer/penpot.ts:327)

5. **Some visible content is skipped entirely.** Traversal stops when an element has no bounding box. That drops descendants of `display: contents` and zero-sized wrappers with visible overflow. Separate “this element paints something” from “visit its children.” [extractor.ts:21](/home/peterc/ultimate-html-penpot-ext/src/capture/extractor.ts:21)

6. **Text capture destroys meaningful whitespace.** Text is compacted and trimmed regardless of `white-space`. Code blocks lose indentation, and spaces around inline spans can disappear. Capture whitespace according to its computed CSS behavior, including nonbreaking spaces. [extractor.ts:19](/home/peterc/ultimate-html-penpot-ext/src/capture/extractor.ts:19)

7. **Failed images can vanish silently and be retried repeatedly.** Upload exceptions are swallowed, failed results aren’t effectively cached, and an undecorated image rectangle may have no visible fill. Cache failure outcomes, create explicit placeholders, and return asset diagnostics to the UI. [penpot.ts:263](/home/peterc/ultimate-html-penpot-ext/src/importer/penpot.ts:263)

There’s also a product-level limitation: **the responsive boards are fixed snapshots.** Flex/grid metadata is captured but isn’t used to create native Penpot layouts. Selective layout conversion could improve editability after the fidelity bugs are addressed.

All **124 tests pass**, but the extractor tests mostly check that generated JavaScript contains particular strings; they don’t exercise browser layout. I’d add browser fixtures covering these cases before expanding CSS support. [extractor.test.ts:4](/home/peterc/ultimate-html-penpot-ext/src/capture/extractor.test.ts:4)

My first implementation pass would cover background images, clipping, and transparency. Those affect common page designs and have clear regression cases. This was a code review only; no files changed, and visual behavior hasn’t been verified in a live Penpot session.
